title: Ice on Lake Mendota

data.source: North Temperate Lakes LTER, Ice Duration, Madison Lakes Area (Magnuson, Carpenter and Stanley 2021, doi:10.6073/pasta/ab31f2489ee436beb73fc8f1d0213d97), as packaged in lterdatasampler
data.licence: CC0 (lterdatasampler); source data package CC BY 4.0 (EDI)

prediction: With trends removed, the ice-out date follows the freeze-up date of the same winter with a slope above 0.5 (P-OWN); and the seed rule forecasts next winter's days of ice better than persistence, the running mean, the 30-winter normal and a trend line (P-SEED).
baseline: An outside clock (slope 0); persistence, the running mean, the mean of the last 30 winters, and a straight-line trend.
why: Ice-out did not follow freeze-up, so the lake keeps no count of its own. But the seed rule did beat persistence, the running mean, the 30-winter normal and the trend line when forecasting the days of ice.
